title: Derivative as density times score
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $v\ge 0$, and let $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$. The derivative of the product Gaussian density with respect to its mean, viewed as a linear functional on $\mathbb R^I$, equals the product density multiplied by the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. For $c,z,h\in\mathbb R^I$, $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$.
